title: 12. Interview: LangChain / LangGraph Checkpointers: Complete Explanations and Examples
summary: Interview Q&A for LangChain / LangGraph Checkpointers: Complete Explanations and Examples.
objectives: Answer the LangChain / LangGraph Checkpointers: Complete Explanations and Examples interview questions out loud
Lead with the concept, then a small example, then a tradeoff

sections.title: Twenty interview questions with direct answers
sections.body:
1. **What is a checkpointer?** A storage adapter that persists graph execution
   records so a thread can be inspected or continued later.
2. **Is it a LangChain or LangGraph feature?** The persistence interface is from
   LangGraph; current LangChain agents use it through their graph implementation.
3. **Is saving messages enough?** No. Recovery also needs runtime scheduling
   information, versions, parent identity and pending task writes.
4. **What is the difference between state and StateSnapshot?** State is application
   data; StateSnapshot also exposes execution position and persistence metadata.
5. **What is a thread?** A persistent conversation/workflow identity spanning
   invocations. It is not inherently a user ID or an authentication credential.
6. **Why are namespaces needed?** To separate graph execution contexts, especially
   nested graphs, within a thread.
7. **What happens with a new InMemorySaver per request?** Each request gets empty
   RAM storage and cannot read the prior saver's history.
8. **When are full checkpoints created?** At execution boundaries governed by
   the runtime/durability mode; task writes can also be saved within a round.
9. **Why implement put_writes?** It records completed task outputs so recovery
   can preserve successful work from a partially failed execution round.
10. **How do you resume a failure?** Fix the cause and normally invoke with `None`
    using the saved thread/config, rather than submit the original input again.
11. **How do you resume a dynamic interrupt?** Use `Command(resume=...)` with the
    same thread and an appropriately validated response.
12. **Does interrupted Python resume at the next line without replay?** The node
    restarts; code before the interrupt can execute again.
13. **Does replay mean no model calls?** No. Work after the selected checkpoint
    executes again and may produce different results.
14. **Does update_state mutate old checkpoints?** It creates a new checkpoint;
    updates are applied through the relevant state writers/reducers.
15. **Can built-in Postgres tables live in my schema?** Yes, with correctly
    configured connections/search path. Their built-in table layout stays intact.
16. **Can I give PostgresSaver any table name?** Not through a generic table-name
    constructor argument in the pinned version. Use a custom backend when required.
17. **Does async persistence guarantee no lost work?** No. Durability mode,
    storage guarantees and crash timing all matter.
18. **Does checkpointing guarantee exactly-once side effects?** No. External
    operations need their own idempotency/coordination design.
19. **How is Store different?** Store holds application-defined data across
    threads; the checkpointer tracks one thread's execution history.
20. **How do you validate a custom saver?** Test reconnect/restart, exact/latest
    reads, history/forks, interrupts, partial failure, writes ordering, deletion,
    async behavior and database-specific transaction/concurrency behavior.
